before: Al-Layth said: Ja'far ibn Rabi'a narrated to me, from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), that he mentioned a man from the Children of Israel. He asked another Israelite to lend him money, and he gave it to him until a specified term. Then he mentioned the hadith: The borrower placed the money in a piece of wood and sent it across the sea when he could find no ship, and Allah delivered it to the lender.
arabic: وَقَالَ اللَّيْثُ حَدَّثَنِي جَعْفَرُ بْنُ رَبِيعَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ هُرْمُزَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ ذَكَرَ رَجُلاً مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ ـ وَسَاقَ الْحَدِيثَ ـ ‏"‏فَخَرَجَ يَنْظُرُ لَعَلَّ مَرْكَبًا قَدْ جَاءَ بِمَالِهِ، فَإِذَا هُوَ بِالْخَشَبَةِ فَأَخَذَهَا لأَهْلِهِ حَطَبًا، فَلَمَّا نَشَرَهَا وَجَدَ الْمَالَ وَالصَّحِيفَةَ ‏"‏‏.‏
after: Al-Layth said: Ja'far ibn Rabi'a narrated to me, from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), that he mentioned a man from the Children of Israel. And he related the hadith: ‘He went out, looking in case a ship had arrived with his money. Then there was the piece of wood, and he took it home as firewood. When he split it open, he found the money and the letter.’
